tool_signatures.name: qa_click_point
tool_signatures.description: Click at an x,y POINT instead of at an element — for applications that draw their interface inside a canvas, where there is nothing to name: Figma, Miro, maps, charts, diagram and image editors. Everywhere else use qa_click: it names what it pressed, survives a re-render and tells you when it missed, none of which a coordinate can do.

tool_signatures.name: qa_close_tab
tool_signatures.description: Close one tab or a list of them — how you tidy up the isolated logins when a matrix run is finished. Returns which ids closed and which were already gone.

tool_signatures.name: qa_done
tool_signatures.description: CALL THIS WHEN THE WORK IS ACTUALLY OVER — the last check made, the last fix verified, the answer about to be written. The mark on every driven tab the person is NOT looking at then pulses slowly, so somebody who walked away from the screen can see from across the room that it ended. It stops by itself when they look at that tab; there is nothing to dismiss.

tool_signatures.name: qa_draft
tool_signatures.description: THE DRAFT REPORT AS IT STANDS: its title, what kind of document it is, and every line in order with its POSITION — which is what every other draft verb takes.

tool_signatures.name: qa_draft_add
tool_signatures.description: ADD ONE LINE, OR SEVERAL, to the end of the draft — the same block shapes qa_report_build takes, so nothing has to be translated on the way out.

tool_signatures.name: qa_draft_build
tool_signatures.description: BUILD THE DRAFT into a self-contained HTML report — the same assembly qa_report_build does and the same one the panel’s Build button runs, so a document written by hand and one written here are the same document.

tool_signatures.name: qa_draft_clear
tool_signatures.description: THROW THE DRAFT AWAY. There is no undo anywhere in this product, and the draft may be an hour of somebody else’s work — read qa_draft first and say what is in it before calling this.

tool_signatures.name: qa_draft_drop
tool_signatures.description: REMOVE THE LINE AT

tool_signatures.name: qa_draft_edit
tool_signatures.description: REPLACE THE LINE AT

tool_signatures.name: qa_draft_meta
tool_signatures.description: SET THE TITLE, THE KIND, OR BOTH. The title becomes the document’s heading and the name the panel lists it under; leave it empty and the page title is used at build time.

tool_signatures.name: qa_draft_move
tool_signatures.description: MOVE THE LINE AT

tool_signatures.name: qa_drag_point
tool_signatures.description: Press at one point, move, release at another — the other half of canvas work, and the half a click cannot express: moving a shape, marqueeing a selection, panning, drawing a box, dragging a handle. Without it an agent fakes a drag out of two clicks and changes something nobody asked for.

tool_signatures.name: qa_export
tool_signatures.description: Full qa-export/v1 bundle for a page: findings (with selectors), failed requests (with server error bodies), detected form structure, recorded repro steps, env, and isolated-login name. Read this, then fix the underlying issues. Pass tabId (from qa_tabs) to target a specific tab / isolated login.

tool_signatures.name: qa_findings
tool_signatures.description: Findings on a page (console/JS/network/a11y/markup/submit) — each with a CSS selector and detail. Filter by severity; pass tabId (from qa_tabs) to read a specific tab / isolated login.

tool_signatures.name: qa_focus_proof
tool_signatures.description: THE ARGUMENT NOBODY WINS WITH A SCREENSHOT, ended with two numbers. Focus the control and measure what actually changed: which of the four properties that can draw a ring moved (outline, box-shadow, border, colours), and what fraction of the PIXELS differ between the two frames.

tool_signatures.name: qa_focus_tab
tool_signatures.description: Put a tab in front of the person — activate it and raise its window — so they are looking at what you are about to show.

tool_signatures.name: qa_focus_walk
tool_signatures.description: The keyboard route as ONE call: presses Tab repeatedly and records where focus actually lands,

tool_signatures.name: qa_frames
tool_signatures.description: A PAGE IS OFTEN SEVERAL DOCUMENTS, AND THE INTERESTING ONE IS USUALLY NOT THE OUTER ONE. A payment form, an SSO step, a chat widget, a Stripe or 3-D Secure field: each lives in a frame of its own, and a frame from another domain cannot be read from the page around it — that is the same-origin rule and no amount of JavaScript gets past it. Qiksy now runs INSIDE every frame and answers about its own document, which is what makes them readable at all.

tool_signatures.name: qa_gap
tool_signatures.description: SAY WHAT THE BRIDGE COULD NOT DO, IN ONE SENTENCE — and it becomes a line in a file the human reads (~/.qiksy/gaps.jsonl).

tool_signatures.name: qa_hover
tool_signatures.description: Put the pointer on an element AND LEAVE IT THERE, then report what that revealed: a menu that opens on hover, a tooltip, the actions a row only shows under the pointer, the value a chart reads out beneath it. qa_click cannot answer any of those — it presses a millisecond after it hovers, and the press closes what the hover opened.

tool_signatures.name: qa_mock
tool_signatures.description: Override what the app RECEIVES from the network — the thing DevTools calls a local override, driven from here. Set a rule and the page

tool_signatures.name: qa_navigate
tool_signatures.description: Point a tab at a URL and wait until it is loaded and Qiksy is live again — the ready-wait is built in, so the next step can run straight after. Use it to jump between steps of a flow that are not reachable by clicking.

tool_signatures.name: qa_odd_one_out
tool_signatures.description: ONE OF THIRTY IS NOT LIKE THE OTHER TWENTY-NINE. No mockup, no Figma, no setup, no alignment: every element is compared ONLY with its own siblings, read in one instant, so nothing here depends on the window or on matching a design layer to a DOM node — the comparison the market cannot do is the one this skips entirely. It finds the card whose padding is 12 where twenty-nine have 16, the one gap of 14 in a row of 16s, the heading left at a different line-height.

tool_signatures.name: qa_open_isolated
tool_signatures.description: Open a tab with its OWN private session — separate cookies, localStorage, IndexedDB — so a second (or third) user can be logged in at the same time in the same browser. Returns its

tool_signatures.name: qa_open_panel

tool_signatures.name: qa_open_tab

tool_signatures.name: qa_pick_date
tool_signatures.description: Put an EXACT date into a date field in ONE call — including the ones a value cannot be written to.

tool_signatures.name: qa_pick_path
tool_signatures.description: One call for the widgets where a single value takes several interactions: an Ant Design Cascader (country → region → city, a column per level), a TreeSelect with collapsed branches, a menu of submenus, any drill-down.

tool_signatures.name: qa_pick_range
tool_signatures.description: Both ends of a date range in one call, for a control that owns two inputs — Ant Design\

tool_signatures.name: qa_pick_tags
tool_signatures.description: One call for a whole list of tags on a control that has no option list to pick from — Ant Design\

tool_signatures.name: qa_pick_time
tool_signatures.description: A time in one call on a column-based picker — Ant Design\

tool_signatures.name: qa_press
tool_signatures.description: Dispatch a keyboard key (keydown/keypress/keyup) — Enter to submit, Escape to close, Tab to move focus. Without a selector it goes to whatever currently has focus, like a real keyboard. Like qa_click, it returns what changed once the page settled. On a recent extension build the reply also carries

tool_signatures.name: qa_probe
tool_signatures.description: Identify ONE unfamiliar control and get back the verb that drives it. Judges it first by shape — role, tag, name, state and its neighbours — which settles a sectioned date field, a file input, a switch, a slider or a plain field without touching the page at all.

tool_signatures.name: qa_read
tool_signatures.description: Return the RENDERED text of the page under test, or of a single element named by a qa_snapshot ref or a CSS selector.

tool_signatures.name: qa_recipe_apply
tool_signatures.description: Replay a saved flow on the page as it is NOW. Per step it takes its own snapshot, matches every field by accessible name (exact, then truncated, then contains, then the stored cssPath), fills the whole step in ONE batch, attaches the step\

tool_signatures.name: qa_recipe_list
tool_signatures.description: The flows already saved on this machine, newest first: name, host, step count, and the fields of the first step so you can tell them apart.

tool_signatures.name: qa_recipe_save
tool_signatures.description: Write what you just did on this page to a JSON recipe on this machine, so the NEXT run replays it instead of rediscovering it.

tool_signatures.name: qa_reload
tool_signatures.description: Reload the tab as it stands — same address, no URL to pass — and wait until it has loaded AND Qiksy is live in the new document, so the next call needs no sleep.

tool_signatures.name: qa_report
tool_signatures.description: Generate Qiksy

tool_signatures.name: qa_report_build
tool_signatures.description: A SELF-CONTAINED HTML REPORT, built by ENUMERATION. You pass an ordered list of blocks with plain text fields; every scrap of markup, styling, escaping and picture-embedding happens on our side. No template is accepted and none can be — a verb here names an element or a value from a closed list, never a program.

tool_signatures.name: qa_report_drop
tool_signatures.description: REMOVES A SAVED REPORT FROM THE EXTENSION — the row and the document together, because an index that forgets an entry while the megabytes stay is a leak nobody finds.

tool_signatures.name: qa_report_edit
tool_signatures.description: EDIT A FINISHED DOCUMENT: read the blocks it was built from, change them, and build it again UNDER THE SAME NAME — so the shelf keeps one document rather than a family of near copies. This is the same operation the person does in the report editor.

tool_signatures.name: qa_report_get
tool_signatures.description: THE DOCUMENT ITSELF, by the name qa_reports lists. Pass

tool_signatures.name: qa_reports
tool_signatures.description: EVERY SAVED REPORT, BY NAME, with its title, what kind it is, when it was built, how many blocks and pictures went in and how big it is.

tool_signatures.name: qa_run_audit
tool_signatures.description: Run Qiksy\

tool_signatures.name: qa_screenshot
tool_signatures.description: Take a real picture of the page under test, or of ONE element, and hand it back as an image you can look at — not as measurements.

tool_signatures.name: qa_shot_crop
tool_signatures.description: SET OR CLEAR THE REGION a shot exports. The crop is a rectangle remembered beside the marks, NOT applied to the bitmap — so the edge can be pulled back out afterwards, by you or by the tester, and «a bit more on the left» never means «take the screenshot again».

tool_signatures.name: qa_shot_drop
tool_signatures.description: REMOVE ONE SHOT, with its marks and its stored image. The shelf holds twenty and drops the oldest by itself, so this is for the ones you know are finished with — a shelf full of half-remembered pictures is the state where nobody can find the one that mattered. The reply names what is left.

tool_signatures.name: qa_shot_list
tool_signatures.description: EVERY SHOT THE PANEL IS HOLDING, by name, with its size, its address, how many marks it carries and whether it is cropped.

tool_signatures.name: qa_shot_mark
tool_signatures.description: ADD MARKS TO A SHOT ON THE SHELF. They are stored beside the clean image, never burned into it, so the tester can move them, resize them and delete them afterwards — and so you can read them back later.

tool_signatures.name: qa_shot_read
tool_signatures.description: THE MARKS, NOT THE PIXELS. Returns every mark on the named shot — kind, position, colour, caption — plus its crop rectangle and its true size.

tool_signatures.name: qa_snapshot
tool_signatures.description: A compact accessibility / interaction snapshot of the WHOLE page: every interactive control, landmark and heading with a role, an accessible name, its state, and a STABLE ref like [ref=e12].

tool_signatures.name: qa_spotlight
tool_signatures.description: Visually highlight (dim + outline) an element on the page — target it by a qa_snapshot ref (preferred) or a CSS selector — so the human tester can see what the agent is referring to. A non-destructive overlay — it does not click, focus, or modify the element.

tool_signatures.name: qa_status
tool_signatures.description: Health snapshot of a page Qiksy is watching: URL, error/warning/form counts, and its isolated-login name if any. Defaults to the active tab; pass tabId (from qa_tabs) to target a specific tab.

tool_signatures.name: qa_storage
tool_signatures.description: Read and write the app

tool_signatures.name: qa_styles
tool_signatures.description: The COMPUTED styles of one element — colour, type, spacing, border, shadow, layout — plus its box in CSS pixels, and the CSS custom properties (design tokens) in scope for it.

tool_signatures.name: qa_suite_run
tool_signatures.description: Replay a GROUP of saved flows back to back and answer about the whole set: which passed, which stopped, at what step and on what.

tool_signatures.name: qa_tabs
tool_signatures.description: List the browser tabs Qiksy can read, including which are ISOLATED multi-login sessions (isolatedSession = the login name). Use a tab\

tool_signatures.name: qa_tour
tool_signatures.description: Return a generated per-page exploratory-testing checklist (from detected forms + interactive surfaces), with items auto-checked from the recorded session. Great raw material for writing test cases. Returns markdown + structured items.

tool_signatures.name: qa_type
tool_signatures.description: Put a value into ONE control, whatever kind it is — target it by a qa_snapshot ref (preferred) or a CSS selector.

tool_signatures.name: qa_type_many
tool_signatures.description: Fill an ENTIRE form (or one step of a wizard) in ONE call instead of a round-trip per field: pass an array of { ref | selector, value, action? }.

tool_signatures.name: qa_upload
tool_signatures.description: Put a file into an <input type=file> — including the hidden ones behind a styled dropzone, which a click can never reach.

tool_signatures.name: qa_wait_for
tool_signatures.description: Wait until the page satisfies ONE named condition, then return — instead of polling qa_snapshot, which renumbers every ref each time it is called.

tool_signatures.name: qa_wait_ready
tool_signatures.description: Block until the tab has finished loading AND Qiksy is live in the new document. Call this after anything that navigates — a submit, a link click, qa_navigate — before the next qa_type/qa_click, or the call lands on a page that is still being replaced. Read-only: waiting is not acting, so this needs no Pro and no consent.

tool_signatures.name: qa_watch
tool_signatures.description: THE ONE QUESTION THE OTHER VERBS CANNOT ANSWER: what happens over the next few seconds.

tool_signatures.name: qa_width_law
tool_signatures.description: THE LAW, NOT THE READING. «The container is 1360 wide» is a fact about the window it was measured in, true here and false one drag of the mouse later — which is why comparing a layout to a mockup by measuring has never worked. This reads what the CODE DECLARED instead: how many width ceilings exist on the layout spine, which element sets the tightest one, and what content band follows from that at any window. A declaration does not move when the window does, so it can be compared with a mockup and argued about.

tool_signatures.name: qa_wiring
tool_signatures.description: A FORM WITH THREE RED MESSAGES UNDER THREE FIELDS LOOKS CORRECT TO EVERYONE WHO CAN SEE IT. That is the illusion: being NEAR a field is not being attached to it, and assistive technology reads the attachment. Somebody filling the form by ear is told «Email» and nothing else, while «Enter a valid email address» sits in red an inch below, invisible to them.
